Tesla Roadster Gets the Most Appropriate Digital Makeover: Back to the Future Has Entered the Chat
44 photos
Photo: ildar_project / Instagram
Almost a decade – close to nine years, more precisely – was the time Tesla took to present the second-generation Roadster from the concept state into ‘reality.’ Ahem, right now, some folks don’t believe this is a real car because of the mind-bending stunts presented at the SpaceX compound in Texas.
Last night (October 15, 2026) Tesla showed at the home of SpaceX their much-hyped electric sports car , the second-generation Roadster, which now may be finally ready for prime time… around 2028. According to Musk, this will be the last non-autonomous car Tesla makes, though the prototype that did all the stunts wasn’t driven by anyone.
But how did it do that? Through suction and cold-gas thrusters, according to the company – and through various fake stuff, according to the Internet, which now debates whether the prototype was an actual car or a shell that was mastered by Hollywood stunt guys from the background.
Anyway, stunts aside, one thing is for sure: the new Tesla Roadster looks nothing like the concept … and it’s also not a roadster. The sleek concept from 2017 still has a remarkably clean design that holds up very well to the test of time, but the new one abandons that for an angular page out of Lamborghini’s wedge-shaped supercars.
There are Lambo-style doors, of course, and it’s a clean-sheet redesign that was well kept under wraps before the presentation – but anyone can also recognize the Cybertruck influence without looking twice. There’s also aerospace influence from the SR-71 Blackbird and the F-35 fighter jet to go along with those rocket boosters, by the way.
Naturally, everyone is currently having an opinion or two about the EV that could star in a Sci-Fi show or movie at Hollywood. That includes the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI, of course. As the Internet has gone wild about the Tesla Roadster, here’s Ildar, the virtual artist better known as " ildar_project " on social media, who usually plays with tuned vehicles - so anyone should be really surprised by this new creation.
That’s because the pixel master has done the only thing acceptable to the new Tesla Roadster… and turned it into the space age heir of the DeLorean from Back to the Future. Now, if only we could convince Marty McFly and Doc Brown to come back for a new installment in the series, everything would be peachy… Do you see Christopher Lloyd and Michael J. Fox reprising their roles alongside Crispin Glover and the rest of the cast or not?
